cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing a letter to Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). Now Paul brings up a problem. What if anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching?
Paul says this teacher is conceited, and he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words. You know when the group chat hits FORTY messages, all fighting over ONE word?

cards.question: Paul says the person teaching against the sound words of Jesus really understands the truth and just explains it badly.
Paul says something comes out of all those disputes about words. What is it?

answers.text: Envy and strife and evil suspicions

cards.text: And it never lets up, friend: constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. Then Paul says these men have their own idea of what godliness is for.

cards.question: Paul is describing men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. What do they think godliness is for?

cards.text: Here's the twist, friend. Paul says, "Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain."
Then Paul explains why. And he goes ALL the way back to the day you showed up in this world.

cards.question: Paul talks about coming into the world and leaving it. What does he say we bring in and carry out?

answers.text: Nothing in and a little out
A little in and nothing out

cards.text: I came out of a bakery's clearance bin with a 25-cent price sticker on me, and that sticker was my WHOLE estate. Then Paul names two things we will be content with.

cards.question: Paul says if we have food and ___ we will be content with these.

cards.text: Then Paul looks down the other road: people who want to be rich.

cards.question: Paul says those who want to be rich fall into ___.

cards.text: And they get ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires. Ensnared, friend, like me the day my mustache got caught in the dough mixer and I went around and AROUND and AROUND.

cards.question: Paul says the foolish and harmful desires of those who want to be rich plunge them into ruin and destruction.

cards.text: Then Paul digs all the way down to the root under all of it.

cards.question: Paul says the ___ of money is the root of all kinds of evil.
Paul says some people craved money. What happened between them and the faith?

answers.text: They held on to it tightly

cards.question: Paul says those who craved money ended up pierced with many sorrows. Who pierced them?
